chunks: Whoever goes regarding a need without wudu (ablution), and his need is not fulfilled, then let him blame none but himself.

key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: a need, matter, or objective a person seeks to have fulfilled
key_terms.نَفْسَهُ: himself, meaning personal responsibility for the neglect mentioned
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purification before acts of devotion and other important matters

ai.seo_question: Does going to seek one’s needs without wudu (ablution) affect whether they are fulfilled?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches that approaching one’s affairs while in a state of wudu (ablution) is a cause of blessing and facilitation. If a person neglects this adab and then finds his need unmet, he should blame himself rather than others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3578 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Whoever goes to fulfill a need without being in a state of ablution, and his need is not fulfilled, let him blame none but himself."
